teaser.en: Carpenters know a mvure plank by its smell, and its timber is so prized that the tree is now rare in Kenya.

summary.en: *Mvure* is the mvule or iroko, a giant forest tree with a tall clean trunk and one of the finest timbers in Africa. Prized for furniture, doors and boats, it has been cut so heavily that it is now rare in Kenya.

about.en:
*Mvure* is a giant, reaching 30 metres, with a tall, straight trunk free of branches and a high, umbrella-shaped crown. The bark is pale grey and oozes a milky latex when cut. The leaves are large and oval. It drops its leaves in the dry season.

The heartwood is golden-brown and resists termites.

where.en: It grows in lowland, riverine and groundwater forest. At the coast it is only occasional, though it is common around Rabai, inland of Mombasa. Remaining big trees stand mostly in forest remnants.

uses.en:
*Mvure* is a premier timber, used for quality furniture indoors and out, for doors, boats, poles and tool handles. The heartwood resists termites.

The bark is used in traditional medicine.

culture.en: Digo carpenters recognise *mvure* planks by their strong smell. Its seeds have their own name, *tembe za mvure*. Carpenters also take care to tell it apart from *mnguonguo*, the 'false mvule', whose wood looks similar but does not last.

names.en: Pakia, the ICRAF handbook and the Mgombato dictionary all give the Digo name *mvure*, which is also the Giriama name. In Swahili it is *mvule*; the Digo *r* matches the Swahili *l*. Mgombato calls it a hardwood, 'East African teak'. In English it is mvule or iroko.

conservation.en: Mvure is now rare in Kenya because of over-exploitation for its timber.

reason.en: Another timber known by the smell of its planks
Its seeds are also called tembe
A giant of the same fig family

definition.en: The seeds of the mvule tree. They have no use, so they are called 'seeds of …'; the useful timber goes by the tree's own name.

mgombato: mvure1 (mi) type of hardwood tree, East-African teak-tree (Milicia excelsa); mvule.
